page: Microsoft Azure L16s_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine from the Lsv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes a 260 MB L3 cache and is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per core.

A key feature of this server is its bundled local storage, consisting of a 3840 GB NVMe SSD that is Premium Storage capable. In benchmark testing, the L16s_v4 demonstrates strong single-core capabilities, scoring 2162.0 in Geekbench single-core and achieving 31.49 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. Multi-core performance is solid, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 15996.5 and a Passmark CPU score of 26806.09. Memory bandwidth tests show 1241.22 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 120.02 GB/sec for uncached large blocks.

The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which assist in workloads like low-latency AI inference. This is reflected in its top-tier performance of 369.86 tokens/sec for text generation using a small 135M LLM model. Qualitatively, the L16s_v4 offers high resource density by combining a large local NVMe SSD with a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it a cost-efficient choice for data-intensive applications without requiring external storage attachments. It is well-suited for large databases, Redis caching layers, and local data processing pipelines.
description: The Microsoft Azure L16s_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 8 physical cores running at 4.2 GHz. It features 128.0 GB of RAM and a bundled 3840 GB local NVMe SSD, making it highly capable for storage-intensive workloads. The x86_64 architecture supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX, which contribute to strong single-core performance and top-tier text generation speeds of 369.86 tokens/sec on small LLM models. Benchmarks indicate reliable multi-core processing with a Passmark CPU score of 26806.09 and a Redis SET throughput of 22.91 million operations per second. This instance provides a cost-efficient balance of high-capacity local storage and dense memory, making it suitable for relational databases, caching layers, and data-intensive processing tasks.
